questions.q: In def calculate_total_with_tax(subtotal, tax_rate=0.08), what happens if you call calculate_total_with_tax(100)?
options: tax_rate automatically uses its default value of 0.08
It raises an error because tax_rate wasn't provided
tax_rate becomes None
It uses a tax_rate of 0
questions.explain: A default argument is used automatically whenever the caller doesn't supply a value for it.

questions.q: What does calling build_order_summary(customer_name="Marcus Ibeh", order_id=1002) demonstrate?
options: Keyword arguments, which let you name parameters and pass them in any order
Default arguments only
*args collecting extra values
A syntax error, since arguments must be positional
questions.explain: Naming the parameters at the call site lets you pass them in any order, as keyword arguments.

questions.q: Inside a function defined as def total_revenue(*line_totals), what type is line_totals?
options: A tuple of all the positional arguments passed in
A dictionary
A single float value
A list that cannot be looped over
questions.explain: *args collects any number of extra positional arguments into a tuple.

questions.q: Inside a function defined as def build_order_record(order_id, **extra_fields), what type is extra_fields?
options: A dictionary of all the named arguments passed in beyond order_id
A tuple
A list of strings
An integer count of how many arguments were passed
questions.explain: **kwargs collects any number of extra named arguments into a dict.

questions.q: Why would a function signature like def build_order_record(order_id, **extra_fields) be useful for building a record?
options: It allows a few required fields plus any number of additional named fields without redefining the function
It prevents the function from ever being called with more than one argument
It converts all arguments into strings automatically
It is required syntax for any function with more than one parameter
questions.explain: **kwargs gives a function flexibility to accept a varying number of named fields, similar to real records.
